# Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(tibble)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(WGCNA)
})
options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
source("R/wto_fast.R")   # vectorised wTO, identical output to wTO::wTO.fast()

pal <- list(bg = "#1A1618", rose = "#EEB4C8", teal = "#64D2D2", gold = "#F2C66D",
            muted = "#8B7780", text = "#D7CBD0", paper = "#F3E9ED",
            plum = "#A35876", dteal = "#318080", line = "#4A303A", soft = "#C0B4B8")

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13) + theme(
  text = element_text(color = "#E5DADA"),
  plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", color = pal$rose),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(color = pal$soft),
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = pal$bg, color = NA),
  panel.background = element_rect(fill = pal$bg, color = NA),
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major = element_line(color = pal$line, linewidth = 0.35),
  axis.text = element_text(color = "#E5DADA"),
  axis.title = element_text(color = pal$soft),
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.background = element_rect(fill = pal$bg, color = NA),
  legend.key = element_rect(fill = pal$bg, color = NA)
))
grp_levels <- c("Control", "no Lithium", "Lithium")
cond_cols <- c(Control = pal$gold, `no Lithium` = pal$teal, Lithium = pal$rose)
```

# Data and quality control

The data are whole-blood RNA-seq from **GSE124326** (Krebs *et al.*, 2020):
112 **controls** and 226 patients with bipolar I disorder, 152 taking
**lithium** and 74 not taking it. Three groups give three networks.
The prepared file holds log2-CPM values (genes x samples) and one row of
metadata per sample, including sex, sequencing plate, and estimated blood-cell
fractions.

```{r}
#| label: load
course_data <- readRDS("data/gse124326_bd_lithium.rds")
expression_matrix <- course_data$expression   # genes x samples, log2-CPM
sample_info <- course_data$sample_info
stopifnot(identical(sample_info$sample, colnames(expression_matrix)))
dim(expression_matrix)
head(sample_info[, c("sample", "treatment", "sex", "plate", "neutrophils")])
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 1 · What drives the main axes of variation?"}
Count the samples per condition and per sex. Run a PCA on the 500 most variable
genes and colour it by **treatment**, **sex**, and **plate** in turn. Which
variable lines up with PC1 or PC2?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex1-task
#| eval: false
table(sample_info$treatment, sample_info$___)

raw_variance <- apply(expression_matrix, 1, var)
top500 <- names(sort(raw_variance, decreasing = TRUE))[1:___]
pca <- prcomp(t(expression_matrix[top500, ]), scale. = TRUE)
pca_data <- cbind(sample_info, PC1 = pca$x[, 1], PC2 = pca$x[, 2])
ggplot(pca_data, aes(PC1, PC2, color = ___)) + geom_point()
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex1-solution
table(sample_info$treatment, sample_info$sex)

raw_variance <- apply(expression_matrix, 1, var)
top500 <- names(sort(raw_variance, decreasing = TRUE))[1:500]
pca <- prcomp(t(expression_matrix[top500, ]), scale. = TRUE)
pca_data <- cbind(sample_info, PC1 = pca$x[, 1], PC2 = pca$x[, 2])
pca_long <- pca_data |>
  select(PC1, PC2, treatment, sex, plate) |>
  pivot_longer(c(treatment, sex, plate), names_to = "variable", values_to = "level")
ggplot(pca_long, aes(PC1, PC2, color = level)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.6, alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable) +
  labs(title = "PCA of the 500 most variable genes", color = NULL)
```

**Sequencing plate** drives PC1, the largest axis of variation. Sex barely
shows on the first two PCs, even though `XIST` is the single most variable gene:
one gene does not make a principal component. Lithium does **not** dominate the
main axes either; its effect is real but small per gene. Plate and sex go into
the limma model and are removed before building networks.
:::

# Gene selection

Network methods scale with the square of the number of genes, and genes that
barely vary contribute mostly noise correlations. We first remove the plate
and sex effects (keeping the group effects), keep **expressed** genes (mean
log-CPM ≥ 2; at low counts, log values vary mostly by sampling noise), and then
keep the **2,000 most variable** of them. This filter ignores the condition labels, so later
module–trait associations are not built in by the selection.

```{r}
#| label: select-genes
treatment_design <- model.matrix(~ factor(treatment, levels = grp_levels), data = sample_info)
adjusted_matrix <- limma::removeBatchEffect(
  expression_matrix, batch = sample_info$plate,
  covariates = model.matrix(~ sex, data = sample_info)[, -1, drop = FALSE],
  design = treatment_design)
expressed <- rowMeans(expression_matrix) >= 2   # drop low, noisy genes first
gene_variance <- apply(adjusted_matrix[expressed, ], 1, var)
selected_genes <- names(sort(gene_variance, decreasing = TRUE))[1:2000]
network_matrix <- adjusted_matrix[selected_genes, ]
dat_expr <- t(network_matrix)   # samples x genes for WGCNA and ARACNE
dim(dat_expr)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 2 · Why adjust, and why filter by variance?"}
(a) What are the variance and the variance rank of `XIST` before and after
adjustment?
(b) Compare absolute gene–gene correlations for the 2,000 selected genes and
2,000 random genes. Which set correlates more strongly? Correlate the first
principal component of each set with the estimated neutrophil fraction: what
drives the correlation?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex2-task
#| eval: false
rank_of <- function(v, g) match(g, names(sort(v, decreasing = TRUE)))
c(before = rank_of(raw_variance, "XIST"), after = rank_of(___, "XIST"))

set.seed(1)
random_genes <- sample(rownames(adjusted_matrix), ___)
abs_cor <- function(genes) {
  C <- cor(t(adjusted_matrix[genes, ]))
  abs(C[upper.tri(C)])
}
summary(abs_cor(selected_genes))
summary(abs_cor(___))
pc1 <- function(genes) prcomp(t(adjusted_matrix[genes, ]), scale. = TRUE)$x[, 1]
cor(pc1(random_genes), sample_info$___)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex2-solution
rank_of <- function(v, g) match(g, names(sort(v, decreasing = TRUE)))
tibble(when = c("before", "after"),
       variance = round(c(raw_variance["XIST"], gene_variance["XIST"]), 2),
       rank = c(rank_of(raw_variance, "XIST"), rank_of(gene_variance, "XIST")))

set.seed(1)
random_genes <- sample(rownames(adjusted_matrix), 2000)
abs_cor <- function(genes) {
  C <- cor(t(adjusted_matrix[genes, ]))
  abs(C[upper.tri(C)])
}
cor_cmp <- bind_rows(
  tibble(set = "Top 2,000 by variance", r = abs_cor(selected_genes)),
  tibble(set = "Random 2,000", r = abs_cor(random_genes))
)
cor_cmp |> group_by(set) |> summarise(median = median(r), q90 = quantile(r, 0.9))

ggplot(cor_cmp, aes(r, fill = set)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6, color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(pal$muted, pal$gold)) +
  labs(title = "Absolute gene–gene correlation", x = "|r|", y = "Density", fill = NULL)

pc1 <- function(genes) prcomp(t(adjusted_matrix[genes, ]), scale. = TRUE)$x[, 1]
c(random_pc1_vs_neutrophils   = cor(pc1(random_genes), sample_info$neutrophils),
  selected_pc1_vs_neutrophils = cor(pc1(selected_genes), sample_info$neutrophils))
```

(a) Adjustment removes the female–male difference, so `XIST` loses most of its
variance; it still varies between women and may stay in the top 2,000.
(b) The random genes correlate **more**, and the first PC of **both** sets
follows the neutrophil fraction (a PC's sign is arbitrary, so read |r|). In whole blood, the mix of cell types moves thousands of
genes up and down together. Strong correlation is not automatically interesting
structure: ask what drives it. That cell-mix axis is also why the lithium
contrast, which raises neutrophils, needs care.
:::

# Differential expression with limma

limma tests **all** expressed genes, with sex and plate as covariates. One model
answers two questions: **lithium** (on vs off lithium, within bipolar disorder)
and **diagnosis** (patients off lithium vs controls, so the drug does not leak
into the disease contrast). `trend = TRUE` lets the prior variance follow mean
expression, as recommended for log-CPM data.

```{r}
#| label: limma
group_factor <- factor(sample_info$treatment, levels = grp_levels)
design <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group_factor + sex + plate, data = sample_info)
colnames(design) <- make.names(sub("group_factor", "", colnames(design)))
contrasts <- limma::makeContrasts(lithium = Lithium - no.Lithium,
                                  diagnosis = no.Lithium - Control, levels = design)
fit <- limma::lmFit(expression_matrix, design)
fit <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit, contrasts), trend = TRUE)
limma_results <- limma::topTable(fit, coef = "lithium", number = Inf)       # BH
diagnosis_results <- limma::topTable(fit, coef = "diagnosis", number = Inf)
head(limma_results)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 3 · Covariates change the answer"}
(a) How many genes pass FDR < 0.05 for lithium, and for diagnosis? How many
lithium DEGs also have |logFC| > 0.5?
(b) Re-fit the lithium contrast **without** sex and plate. How many genes pass now?
(c) How many of the 2,000 network genes are lithium DEGs?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex3-task
#| eval: false
sum(limma_results$adj.P.Val < ___)
sum(___$adj.P.Val < 0.05)
sum(limma_results$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & abs(limma_results$logFC) > ___)

design0 <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group_factor)
colnames(design0) <- c("Control", "no.Lithium", "Lithium")
fit0 <- limma::lmFit(expression_matrix, ___)
fit0 <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit0, limma::makeContrasts(
  Lithium - no.Lithium, levels = design0)), trend = TRUE)
sum(limma::topTable(fit0, number = Inf)$adj.P.Val < 0.05)

sum(limma_results[___, "adj.P.Val"] < 0.05)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex3-solution
deg <- rownames(limma_results)[limma_results$adj.P.Val < 0.05]
design0 <- model.matrix(~ 0 + group_factor)
colnames(design0) <- c("Control", "no.Lithium", "Lithium")
fit0 <- limma::lmFit(expression_matrix, design0)
fit0 <- limma::eBayes(limma::contrasts.fit(fit0, limma::makeContrasts(
  Lithium - no.Lithium, levels = design0)), trend = TRUE)
c(lithium_fdr_0.05 = length(deg),
  diagnosis_fdr_0.05 = sum(diagnosis_results$adj.P.Val < 0.05),
  fdr_and_lfc_0.5 = sum(limma_results$adj.P.Val < 0.05 & abs(limma_results$logFC) > 0.5),
  without_covariates = sum(limma::topTable(fit0, number = Inf)$adj.P.Val < 0.05),
  degs_in_network = sum(selected_genes %in% deg))

ggplot(limma_results, aes(logFC, -log10(P.Value), color = adj.P.Val < 0.05)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#5E4E56", `TRUE` = pal$rose),
                     labels = c("FDR ≥ 0.05", "FDR < 0.05")) +
  labs(title = "Lithium vs no lithium (adjusted for sex and plate)", color = NULL)
```

Thousands of genes pass FDR for lithium, but few change by more than ~1.4-fold:
with 338 samples, small shifts are detectable. The diagnosis contrast finds
fewer. Leaving out sex and plate adds noise and changes the answer. DEGs are **under-represented** among the most variable
genes (`r round(100 * mean(selected_genes %in% deg))`% of the network genes vs
`r round(100 * length(deg) / nrow(limma_results))`% genome-wide): in blood,
variance is dominated by differences between people (HLA genotype, cell mix),
not by lithium. We come back to this overlap at the end.
:::

# WGCNA

```{r}
#| label: wgcna
invisible(capture.output(power_fit <- WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold(
  dat_expr, powerVector = c(1:10, seq(12, 20, 2)), networkType = "signed", verbose = 0)))
soft_power <- power_fit$powerEstimate   # lowest power with scale-free R^2 >= 0.85
soft_power
wgcna_fit <- WGCNA::blockwiseModules(
  dat_expr, power = soft_power, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed",
  minModuleSize = 20, mergeCutHeight = 0.25, maxBlockSize = 5000,
  randomSeed = 20261109, verbose = 0
)
module_colors <- as.character(wgcna_fit$colors)  # already colour names
names(module_colors) <- colnames(dat_expr)
module_eigengenes <- WGCNA::orderMEs(wgcna_fit$MEs)
table(module_colors)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 4 · Sensitivity to the soft threshold"}
Re-run WGCNA with `power = 6`, below the scale-free plateau. How many modules do you get, and how large is
the grey (unassigned) group? What does a lower power do to weak links?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex4-task
#| eval: false
fit12 <- WGCNA::blockwiseModules(
  dat_expr, power = ___, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed",
  minModuleSize = 20, mergeCutHeight = 0.25, maxBlockSize = 5000,
  randomSeed = 20261109, verbose = 0
)
table(as.character(fit12$colors))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex4-solution
fit12 <- WGCNA::blockwiseModules(
  dat_expr, power = 6, networkType = "signed", TOMType = "signed",
  minModuleSize = 20, mergeCutHeight = 0.25, maxBlockSize = 5000,
  randomSeed = 20261109, verbose = 0
)
cmp <- tibble(
  power = c(soft_power, 6),
  modules = c(length(setdiff(unique(module_colors), "grey")),
              length(setdiff(unique(as.character(fit12$colors)), "grey"))),
  grey_genes = c(sum(module_colors == "grey"),
                 sum(as.character(fit12$colors) == "grey"))
)
cmp
```

The power changes the partition: here β = 6 gives
`r cmp$modules[2]` modules and `r cmp$grey_genes[2]` grey genes, against
`r cmp$modules[1]` and `r cmp$grey_genes[1]` at β = `r soft_power`. A lower power
keeps more weak correlations, so the topological overlap is flatter and branch
boundaries in the tree shift. Module boundaries are a **choice**, so report
them.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 5 · Module–trait association and hubs"}
Which module eigengene correlates most strongly with lithium treatment? List
its 10 genes with the highest module membership (kME).
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex5-task
#| eval: false
case_indicator <- as.numeric(sample_info$treatment == "Lithium")
module_trait <- cor(module_eigengenes, ___)
mt <- module_trait[rownames(module_trait) != "MEgrey", , drop = FALSE]  # skip unassigned
top_module <- rownames(mt)[which.max(abs(mt[, 1]))]
kme <- WGCNA::signedKME(dat_expr, module_eigengenes)
top_color <- sub("^ME", "", top_module)
in_mod <- module_colors == top_color
kme_mod <- setNames(kme[[paste0("kME", ___)]], rownames(kme))[in_mod]
head(sort(kme_mod, decreasing = TRUE), 10)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex5-solution
case_indicator <- as.numeric(sample_info$treatment == "Lithium")
module_trait <- cor(module_eigengenes, case_indicator)
module_trait[order(-abs(module_trait[, 1])), , drop = FALSE]
mt <- module_trait[rownames(module_trait) != "MEgrey", , drop = FALSE]  # skip unassigned
top_module <- rownames(mt)[which.max(abs(mt[, 1]))]
kme <- WGCNA::signedKME(dat_expr, module_eigengenes)
top_color <- sub("^ME", "", top_module)
in_mod <- module_colors == top_color
kme_mod <- setNames(kme[[paste0("kME", top_color)]], rownames(kme))[in_mod]
hubs <- head(sort(kme_mod, decreasing = TRUE), 10)
tibble(gene = names(hubs), kME = round(hubs, 3))
```

These intramodular hubs are the genes most representative of the module's
expression pattern; they are candidates, not proven regulators.
:::

# ARACNE

```{r}
#| label: aracne
mi_matrix <- minet::build.mim(dat_expr, estimator = "spearman")
aracne_matrix <- minet::aracne(mi_matrix, eps = 0)
aracne_degree <- rowSums(aracne_matrix > 0)
c(edges = sum(aracne_matrix > 0) / 2)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 6 · Do ARACNE hubs and WGCNA hubs agree?"}
Take the 50 genes with the highest ARACNE degree. Which WGCNA modules do they
belong to? How many of the trait-associated module's top-50 kME genes are also
ARACNE hubs?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex6-task
#| eval: false
aracne_hubs <- names(sort(aracne_degree, decreasing = TRUE))[1:___]
table(module_colors[aracne_hubs])
kme_top50 <- names(head(sort(kme_mod, decreasing = TRUE), 50))  # whole module if smaller
length(intersect(___, ___))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex6-solution
aracne_hubs <- names(sort(aracne_degree, decreasing = TRUE))[1:50]
table(module_colors[aracne_hubs])
kme_top50 <- names(head(sort(kme_mod, decreasing = TRUE), 50))  # whole module if smaller
length(intersect(aracne_hubs, kme_top50))
```

Here `r length(intersect(aracne_hubs, kme_top50))` genes are hubs in both. The
two methods define importance differently: a WGCNA hub sits at the centre of
one module, while ARACNE's pruning removes indirect links, so its hubs are genes
with many **direct**, non-redundant partners, often bridging modules (look at
the module table above). Little overlap is common; genes found by both are the
more robust candidates.
:::

# wTO networks per group

wTO is computed **separately** for each group (controls, patients off lithium,
patients on lithium) on all 2,000 genes with 100
bootstrap resamples. The p-value measures stability: the share of resamples in
which a link moved by more than `delta = 0.2`.

```{r}
#| label: wto
wto_nets <- load_wto_networks(network_matrix, sample_info, n = 100)
sapply(wto_nets[c("control", "no_lithium", "lithium")],
       function(x) sum(x$pval.adj < 0.05))   # stable links per group
head(wto_nets$lithium)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 7 · Strongest links and sign flips"}
List the 10 strongest links (largest |wTO|) among stable links
(`pval.adj < 0.05`) in the control and in the lithium network. How many pairs
are stable in both but have opposite signs?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex7-task
#| eval: false
stable <- function(x) x[x$pval.adj < ___, ]
stable(wto_nets$control) |> arrange(desc(abs(wTO))) |> head(10)
both <- inner_join(stable(wto_nets$control), stable(wto_nets$lithium),
                   by = c("Node.1", "Node.2"), suffix = c(".ctrl", ".li"))
sum(sign(both$wTO.ctrl) != sign(___))
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex7-solution
stable <- function(x) x[x$pval.adj < 0.05, ]
stable(wto_nets$control) |> arrange(desc(abs(wTO))) |> head(10)
stable(wto_nets$lithium) |> arrange(desc(abs(wTO))) |> head(10)
both <- inner_join(stable(wto_nets$control), stable(wto_nets$lithium),
                   by = c("Node.1", "Node.2"), suffix = c(".ctrl", ".li"))
c(stable_in_both = nrow(both),
  sign_flips = sum(sign(both$wTO.ctrl) != sign(both$wTO.li)))
```

Sign flips are the raw material of CoDiNA's **β** class. Lithium was not
randomized, so treat them as hypotheses.
:::

# Consensus network

A consensus asks which links are **robust across related networks**. Patients
off and on lithium share the disease and differ in treatment, so their
consensus is a **bipolar-disorder network** that does not depend on lithium.

```{r}
#| label: consensus
as_wto_input <- function(x) data.frame(Node.1 = factor(x$Node.1), Node.2 = factor(x$Node.2),
                                       wTO = x$wTO, pval = x$pval)
consensus <- wTO::wTO.Consensus(list(as_wto_input(wto_nets$no_lithium),
                                     as_wto_input(wto_nets$lithium)))
head(consensus)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 8 · The bipolar consensus"}
Keep links with |CN| ≥ 0.3 and a BH-adjusted Fisher p < 0.05 (on 2,000 genes, wTO
rarely exceeds 0.4). How many are there? How many of them are **strong
(|ω| ≥ 0.3) and same-signed in both** patient groups, and how many are carried
by only one?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex8-task
#| eval: false
robust <- consensus |>
  mutate(padj = p.adjust(pval.fisher, "BH")) |>
  filter(abs(CN) >= ___, padj < ___)
ab <- inner_join(wto_nets$no_lithium, wto_nets$lithium,
                 by = c("Node.1", "Node.2"), suffix = c(".off", ".on")) |>
  semi_join(robust |> mutate(across(c(Node.1, Node.2), as.character)),
            by = c("Node.1", "Node.2"))
table(agrees = sign(ab$wTO.off) == sign(ab$wTO.on) &
        pmin(abs(ab$wTO.off), abs(ab$wTO.on)) >= ___)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex8-solution
robust <- consensus |>
  mutate(padj = p.adjust(pval.fisher, "BH")) |>
  filter(abs(CN) >= 0.3, padj < 0.05)
nrow(robust)
ab <- inner_join(wto_nets$no_lithium, wto_nets$lithium,
                 by = c("Node.1", "Node.2"), suffix = c(".off", ".on")) |>
  semi_join(robust |> mutate(across(c(Node.1, Node.2), as.character)),
            by = c("Node.1", "Node.2")) |>
  mutate(agrees = sign(wTO.off) == sign(wTO.on) & pmin(abs(wTO.off), abs(wTO.on)) >= 0.3)
table(ab$agrees)
set.seed(3)
ggplot(ab |> slice_sample(n = min(8000, nrow(ab))), aes(wTO.off, wTO.on, color = agrees)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = pal$rose, `TRUE` = pal$gold),
                     labels = c("carried by one group", "agrees in both")) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(title = "Bipolar consensus links: off vs on lithium",
       x = "wTO · no Lithium", y = "wTO · Lithium", color = NULL)
```

Weighting by |ω| lets the stronger network dominate: a link that is strong in
one group and weak in the other still gets a large CN and a small Fisher p.
Always check per-network agreement. The links that agree form the shared
bipolar network; the ones carried by one group are where CoDiNA looks for
treatment effects.
:::

# CoDiNA

With three networks, every link is a point in the cube $[-1,1]^3$ and its class
says **where** it is present: `g.noLithium.Lithium` = both patient groups but
not controls (disease), `g.Lithium` = only on lithium, and so on.

```{r}
#| label: codina
to_codina <- function(x, padj = 0.05) {
  x |> filter(pval.adj < padj) |> transmute(Node.1, Node.2, wTO)
}
codina_input <- lapply(wto_nets[c("control", "no_lithium", "lithium")], to_codina)
codes <- c("Control", "noLithium", "Lithium")
codina_result <- CoDiNA::MakeDiffNet(Data = codina_input, Code = codes,
                                     cutoff = 0.33, stretch = TRUE)
sort(table(codina_result$Phi_tilde), decreasing = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 9 · Why stretch?"}
The three networks come from 112, 74 and 152 samples. Compare their |wTO|
distributions, then re-run `MakeDiffNet()` with `stretch = FALSE`. How do the
γ classes change, and why?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex9-task
#| eval: false
sapply(wto_nets[c("control", "no_lithium", "lithium")],
       function(x) quantile(abs(x$wTO), ___))
codina_raw <- CoDiNA::MakeDiffNet(Data = codina_input, Code = codes,
                                  cutoff = 0.33, stretch = ___)
sort(table(codina_raw$Phi_tilde), decreasing = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex9-solution
sapply(wto_nets[c("control", "no_lithium", "lithium")],
       function(x) quantile(abs(x$wTO), c(0.5, 0.9, 0.99)))
codina_raw <- CoDiNA::MakeDiffNet(Data = codina_input, Code = codes,
                                  cutoff = 0.33, stretch = FALSE)
full_join(as.data.frame(table(Phi_tilde = codina_result$Phi_tilde)),
          as.data.frame(table(Phi_tilde = codina_raw$Phi_tilde)),
          by = "Phi_tilde", suffix = c(".stretch", ".raw"))
```

The networks do not share one scale: the 74-patient network sits highest
across its whole |wTO| distribution. On the raw scale, links cross the 0.33
threshold most often in that group, so the γ links pile up in `g.noLithium` and
most other classes shrink. `stretch = TRUE` rescales each network by its own
maximum |wTO| before discretizing. Group size is one reason for the different
scales (correlations from fewer samples are noisier, and noise inflates
|r|); real differences in co-expression are another. A stricter check is to
subsample every group to the same size and rebuild the networks.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 10 · From links to genes"}
Use `ClusterNodes()` to assign genes to CoDiNA classes. Which genes are
**disease** genes (`g.noLithium.Lithium`) and which are **lithium-only**
(`g.Lithium`)?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex10-task
#| eval: false
codina_nodes <- CoDiNA::ClusterNodes(codina_result, cutoff.external = ___,
                                     cutoff.internal = ___)
table(codina_nodes$Phi_tilde)
disease_genes <- codina_nodes$Node[codina_nodes$Phi_tilde == ___]
case_genes <- codina_nodes$Node[codina_nodes$Phi_tilde == ___]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex10-solution
codina_nodes <- CoDiNA::ClusterNodes(codina_result, cutoff.external = 0,
                                     cutoff.internal = 1)
sort(table(codina_nodes$Phi_tilde), decreasing = TRUE)
disease_genes <- as.character(codina_nodes$Node[codina_nodes$Phi_tilde == "g.noLithium.Lithium"])
case_genes <- as.character(codina_nodes$Node[codina_nodes$Phi_tilde == "g.Lithium"])
c(disease = length(disease_genes), lithium_only = length(case_genes))
head(disease_genes, 15)
```

`ClusterNodes()` counts each gene's links per class and keeps the class only
when a chi-square test says the links concentrate there (BH < 0.05); otherwise
the gene is "U" (unclassified). Disease genes are connected in **both** patient
groups but not in controls, so lithium cannot explain them; lithium-only genes
gain partners only in treated patients.
:::

# Functional enrichment

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 11 · The background matters"}
Run GO Biological Process ORA on the lithium-only (`g.Lithium`) genes twice: once with the
2,000 network genes as universe, once without a universe (whole annotated
genome). Compare the number of terms with FDR < 0.05.
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex11-task
#| eval: false
to_entrez <- function(symbols) clusterProfiler::bitr(
  symbols, fromType = "SYMBOL", toType = "ENTREZID", OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db)
ora <- function(genes, universe = NULL) clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
  gene = unique(to_entrez(genes)$ENTREZID),
  universe = if (is.null(universe)) NULL else unique(to_entrez(universe)$ENTREZID),
  OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID", ont = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1)
sum(as.data.frame(ora(case_genes, ___))$p.adjust < 0.05)
sum(as.data.frame(ora(case_genes))$p.adjust < 0.05)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex11-solution
to_entrez <- function(symbols) clusterProfiler::bitr(
  symbols, fromType = "SYMBOL", toType = "ENTREZID", OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db)
ora <- function(genes, universe = NULL) clusterProfiler::enrichGO(
  gene = unique(to_entrez(genes)$ENTREZID),
  universe = if (is.null(universe)) NULL else unique(to_entrez(universe)$ENTREZID),
  OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db, keyType = "ENTREZID", ont = "BP",
  pAdjustMethod = "BH", pvalueCutoff = 1, qvalueCutoff = 1)
ora_universe <- ora(case_genes, selected_genes)
ora_genome <- ora(case_genes)
c(network_universe = sum(as.data.frame(ora_universe)$p.adjust < 0.05),
  whole_genome = sum(as.data.frame(ora_genome)$p.adjust < 0.05))
head(as.data.frame(ora_universe)[, c("Description", "GeneRatio", "p.adjust")], 10)
```

The two runs ask different questions. Against the 2,000 network genes:
are the `g.Lithium` genes special **among variable blood genes**? Against the whole
genome: are they special **among all annotated genes**? The genome background
adds thousands of genes and tests, so terms can appear or disappear in either
direction. Always report the universe you used.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 12 · GSEA on module membership"}
Rank all 2,000 genes by kME for the trait-associated module and run `gseGO()`.
Which terms have the largest positive NES?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex12-task
#| eval: false
rank_vec <- sort(setNames(kme[, paste0("kME", ___)], rownames(kme)), decreasing = TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex12-solution
rank_vec <- sort(setNames(kme[, paste0("kME", top_color)], rownames(kme)), decreasing = TRUE)
rank_map <- to_entrez(names(rank_vec))
rank_tbl <- tibble(SYMBOL = names(rank_vec), score = rank_vec) |>
  inner_join(rank_map, by = "SYMBOL") |> distinct(ENTREZID, .keep_all = TRUE)
gene_list <- sort(setNames(rank_tbl$score, rank_tbl$ENTREZID), decreasing = TRUE)
gsea <- clusterProfiler::gseGO(gene_list, OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db,
                               ont = "BP", keyType = "ENTREZID", pvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                               seed = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)
as.data.frame(gsea) |> arrange(desc(NES)) |>
  select(Description, setSize, NES, p.adjust) |> head(10)
```
:::

# Comparing outcomes

::: {.callout-tip title="Exercise 13 · Do DE and networks point at the same genes?"}
For each of the 2,000 network genes, record whether it is a lithium **DEG**
(FDR < 0.05), a **WGCNA hub** of the trait-associated module (top 50 kME), an
**ARACNE hub** (top 50 degree), and **lithium-only** in CoDiNA (`g.Lithium`).
How many genes are flagged by DE only, by a network method only, or by both?
Then ask the disease question: how many CoDiNA disease genes
(`g.noLithium.Lithium`) are **diagnosis** DEGs?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ex13-task
#| eval: false
flags <- tibble(gene = selected_genes) |>
  mutate(DEG = gene %in% ___,
         WGCNA_hub = gene %in% names(head(sort(kme_mod, decreasing = TRUE), 50)),
         ARACNE_hub = gene %in% aracne_hubs,
         CoDiNA_lithium = gene %in% ___)
flags |> mutate(network = WGCNA_hub | ARACNE_hub | CoDiNA_lithium) |> count(DEG, network)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Show solution"}
```{r}
#| label: ex13-solution
wgcna_hubs <- names(head(sort(kme_mod, decreasing = TRUE), 50))
flags <- tibble(gene = selected_genes) |>
  mutate(DEG = gene %in% deg,
         WGCNA_hub = gene %in% wgcna_hubs,
         ARACNE_hub = gene %in% aracne_hubs,
         CoDiNA_lithium = gene %in% case_genes)
flags |> mutate(network = WGCNA_hub | ARACNE_hub | CoDiNA_lithium) |> count(DEG, network)

# DEG rate inside each network gene set vs the 2,000-gene background
flags |>
  summarise(across(c(WGCNA_hub, ARACNE_hub, CoDiNA_lithium),
                   ~ mean(DEG[.x]), .names = "{.col}")) |>
  mutate(all_network_genes = mean(flags$DEG))
flags |> filter(DEG, WGCNA_hub | CoDiNA_lithium) |> head(10)

# the disease question: CoDiNA disease genes vs diagnosis DEGs
dx_deg <- rownames(diagnosis_results)[diagnosis_results$adj.P.Val < 0.05]
c(disease_genes = length(disease_genes),
  also_diagnosis_DEG = sum(disease_genes %in% dx_deg),
  rate_disease_genes = mean(disease_genes %in% dx_deg),
  rate_all_network_genes = mean(selected_genes %in% dx_deg))
```

The methods answer different questions, so the lists overlap only partly.
Genes flagged by **both** DE and a network method are the strongest
candidates; network-only genes are where co-expression adds something DE
cannot see.
:::
